column1: # subject-revisions.tsv — the REQUIRED revision of every out-of-tree subject the close gate scores.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `External/` is gitignored (.gitignore:5), and until 2026-08-08 the revision
# of everything under it was written down NOWHERE: grepping every .md/.sh/.rb/.json in the repo for
# `9c05a72` — the sha External/oss/IceCubesApp has actually been sitting at since 2026-06-09 — found
# zero hits. Every R2 pixel floor in Scripts/icecubes-r2.sh, every rung in IceCubesCheck, and every
# corpus verdict in ProjectCheck is therefore a number ABOUT A TREE NOBODY NAMED. If a subject
# checkout moved (a `git pull` in External/oss/IceCubesApp, a re-clone of a corpus project), each of
# those numbers would silently become a claim about a different program and nothing in the gate
# would notice: the floors would just start reading wrong, and the first suspicion would fall on the
# interpreter. A floor is only a measurement if the thing measured is pinned.
# FORMAT: tab-separated, three columns, `#` comments and blank lines ignored.
#   <subject path, relative to the checkout root> <TAB> <expected git sha> <TAB> <gate consumers>
# TSV, not JSON, on purpose: the enforcing reader is zsh inside a close-gate stage that must run
# before `build`, and `jq` is not guaranteed present on this machine (nothing else in Scripts/
# depends on it). `while IFS=$'\t' read -r ...` parses this with a shell builtin and no parser at
# all; the fields are a filesystem path, a 40-hex sha and a comma list, none of which can contain a
# tab. The three JSON manifests this repo already tracks (Tests/ConcurrencyParity/Manifests/*.json)
# are all read by ruby or Swift, which have parsers; this one is not.
# CONSUMERS column — which close-gate stage reads the subject, so a drift report says what breaks:
#   evaluation     `.build/debug/ProjectCheck --all` walks every directory under External/oss and
#                  scores it as `oss:<name>`; all 94 oss checkouts are gate-scored, and they are 94
#                  of the 680 census units the gate pins by exact match (`678/680`).
#   icecubes-r2    Scripts/icecubes-r2.sh, through the twin's package dependency paths
# Those consumers are cited as GREPS, not as line numbers, and that is not fastidiousness: the
# gate.sh census contract this file leaned on moved ~250 lines (1210 → 1463) within a day of being
# written because two stages were inserted above it, the IceCubesCheck line number quoted in the
# first draft pointed at unrelated code the moment it was written, and its real anchor moved again
# (1450 → 1476) while these very lines were being edited. An out-of-date citation is exactly the
# failure this file exists to end: a claim that outlives the evidence for it.
# HOW TO REGENERATE THE FIRST TWO COLUMNS (the command that produced every sha below, run
# 2026-08-08 from the checkout root; the consumers column is maintained by hand from the four
# references above, because no command derives it):
#   for d in External/oss/*/ External/deps/*/; do p=${d%/}
# There is deliberately NO `--freeze`/`--update` flag on Scripts/verify-subject-revisions.sh. A pin
# that a script can refresh for you is not a pin — it is a log of whatever happened. Moving a sha
# here is an edit, in its own commit, saying which subject moved and what it does to the boards that
# scored the old one (AGENTS.md: "A violation is not a request to move the threshold").
# ABSENCE IS NOT DRIFT. A subject that is not on disk reports `n/a` and scores nothing. The gate
# builds a clean detached worktree and symlinks `External` in, and its board contract sanctions a
# SECOND census — `586/586`, lane-concurrency's environment with External/oss NOT checked out at
# all (`grep -n 'projects pass' Scripts/gate.sh`) — so an environment legitimately missing every
# row below must still be able to close.
# THE REVERSE IS REPORTED, NOT ENFORCED. A directory that is on disk under one of the roots named
# below but has NO row here is scored by ProjectCheck and pinned by nobody; the validator counts it
# as `unpinned` with ceiling n/a and prints it. It cannot be a violation, because adding a checkout
# under External/oss is precisely how a new corpus project is proposed, and this stage runs BEFORE
# the census that would admit it — a validator that red-lit the first step of its own intended
# workflow would be routed around. The count is in the receipt so the coupling between these rows
# and the 94-of-680 census above is visible rather than asserted in a comment.
# LOCAL EDITS. The pin is a HEAD comparison, so a subject with uncommitted TRACKED changes still
# matches its row. Those are reported as `dirty` and, like `unpinned`, score nothing — see the
# hazard note beside `probe_dirty` in Scripts/verify-subject-revisions.sh before making them fatal.
# 95 rows: 94 checkouts under External/oss + 1 under External/deps.
